children: The S&P Global UK Manufacturing PMI eased to 51.7 in August of 2026 from 51.9 in the previous month, the lowest in five months, but revised higher from the flash estimate of 51.5.
Output rose for a fifth month in the period, albeit at the softest pace since April.
New orders grew from both domestic and overseas clients, but the win of new business was concentrated for medium and large-sized companies, which offset weakness in small businesses.

The increase in aggregate levels of new orders drove employment levels to rise the most in two years, gaining traction after companies had cited larger contributions to National Insurance as detriments to their headcounts.
At the same time, supply chain disruptions moderated and input costs rose at the weakest rate in six months.
Looking ahead, half of the companies surveyed were optimistic about the upcoming 12 months.

title: UK Manufacturing Activity Revised Higher
